To fix (4)

To fix Marginal Significance

What we found

You described 1 effect with terms related to ‘marginally significant’.

Show details

You described effects with terms related to ‘marginally significant’. If p values above 0.05 are interpreted as an effect, you inflate the alpha level, and increase the Type 1 error rate. If a p value is higher than the prespecified alpha level, it should be interpreted as a non-significant result.

Text Section Header
Several coefficients in the primary and secondary models were close to the significance threshold. Limitations

For metascientific articles demonstrating the rate at which non-significant p-values are interpreted as marginally significant, see:

Olsson-Collentine A, van Assen MALM, Hartgerink CHJ (2019). “The Prevalence of Marginally Significant Results in Psychology Over Time.” Psychological Science, 30, 576–586. doi:10.1177/0956797619830326.

For the list of terms used to identifify marginally significant results, see this blog post by Matthew Hankins.

To fix Exact P-Values

What we found

We found 4 imprecise p values out of 34 detected p values.

Show details

Reporting p values imprecisely (e.g., p < .05) reduces transparency, reproducibility, and re-use (e.g., in p value meta-analyses). Best practice is to report exact p-values with three decimal places (e.g., p = .032) unless p values are smaller than 0.001, in which case you can use p < .001.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., “decreased at the p < .05 significance threshold”).

P-Value Text
p < .05 The direction of the measurement-format coefficient remained negative in all 38 leave-one-article-out analyses and had p < .05 in 37.
p < .05 None of the three scale contrasts had p < .05 in any article-omission fit.
ps ≥ .087 Mean sample age was positively associated with the age coefficient, b = 0.000230 per year, 95% CI [0.000010, 0.000449], p = .040; the remaining moderator coefficients had ps ≥ .087.
ps ≥ .155 The proportion of female participants was positively associated with the male-minus-female coefficient, b = 0.263 per full-unit difference in female proportion, 95% CI [0.066, 0.461], p = .009, whereas the remaining moderator coefficients had ps ≥ .155.

The APA manual states: Report exact p values (e.g., p = .031) to two or three decimal places. However, report p values less than .001 as p < .001. However, 2 decimals is too imprecise for many use-cases (e.g., a p value meta-analysis), so report p values with three digits.

American Psychological Association (2020). Publication manual of the American Psychological Association, 7 edition. American Psychological Association.

To check (5)

To check Non-Significant P Value Check

What we found

We found 14 non-significant p values that should be checked for appropriate interpretation.

Show details

Meta-scientific research has shown nonsignificant p values are commonly misinterpreted. It is incorrect to infer that there is ‘no effect’, ‘no difference’, or that groups are ‘the same’ after p > 0.05.

It is possible that there is a true non-zero effect, but that the study did not detect it. Make sure your inference acknowledges that it is possible that there is a non-zero effect. It is correct to include the effect is ‘not significantly’ different, although this just restates that p > 0.05.

Metacheck does not yet analyze automatically whether sentences which include non-significant p-values are correct, but we recommend manually checking the sentences below for possible misinterpreted non-significant p values.

README Files

README files are a way to document the contents and structure of a folder, helping users locate the information they need. You can use a README to document changes to a repository, and explain how files are named. Please consider adding a README to each repository or including ‘README’ in the name of your overview document.

Working Directory (setwd)

Best programming practice is to avoid setwd() in analysis code: it hardcodes an assumption about the working directory (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine), so the code breaks when run anywhere else. Keep the working directory as the caller sets it and use relative paths. No setwd() calls were found in any of the code files.

Package Installation (install.packages)

Best programming practice is to avoid install.packages() in analysis code: it installs software on whoever runs the script without asking, which is at minimum disruptive (an unexpected install, network access, a package version the author never tested against) and at worst a security risk if it points at an untrusted repository. Document required packages instead (a README, or a list of them: an renv.lock/DESCRIPTION for R, a requirements.txt for Python). install.packages() calls were found in 3 code files.

This module runs automated data-quality checks (empty columns, SPSS filter variables, category casing, stray whitespace, numbers stored as text, problematic and colliding column names, mixed text encodings, personal information, spreadsheet formatting, and careless responding) on the extracted data files.

We examined 440 columns across 33 data files.

Issues Identified

21 file/column combinations have at least one issue.

About the personal-information flags. These are pattern matches, not confirmed disclosures, and they are tuned to over-report rather than miss something. Expect false positives:

  • Column names are matched against identifying words in English and other European languages (email, telefoonnummer, geboortedatum, …). A column called phone_number flags whether or not it holds one, and an empty or already-anonymised column flags on its name alone.
  • Values are matched against the shape of an identifier. An IP address pattern also matches a version string or a dotted numeric code; a card-number pattern requires both a real issuer prefix and a checksum, but a long numeric ID can still coincide.
  • Free text is flagged when a column holds long, mostly-distinct prose — the shape open-ended answers take. Most such columns contain no names at all.

A flag means look at this column. Where the data is already de-identified (an ip column reading Anonymized, a name column the authors emptied), no action is needed.

Spreadsheet Formatting

We examined 15 spreadsheet files in the repository; 2 have at least one formatting issue.

File Sheet Issue Detail
Open_Alex_Literature_Search_Cleaned.xlsx Tabelle1 Empty or unnamed columns 1 column is empty or has a blank header.
Table5_AdditiveModeratorModels.xlsx NA Not a rectangular dataset This file reads as a table but is not a usable dataset (100% of columns are free text, not variables). Store the data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook.

Spreadsheet formatting such as colour, merged cells, and blank rows/columns is not preserved when data are read programmatically or exported to CSV. Store data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable, no colour-encoded meaning) so it is machine-readable.

Careless Responding

No file could be screened for careless responding.

What this does not cover. Only 0 of 33 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

How to make your code run on another computer

We ran your code on a clean computer, the way a reader or reviewer would. Below is each problem we found, the scripts it affects, and how to fix it. Fix them in the order given: a problem near the top can cause the ones below it.

Files are missing from your deposit.

  • 02_cleaningIPD.R reads raw_data1.csv.

The script stops at the line that reads the file.

  1. Find the file on your computer.
  2. Add it to the deposit, in the folder where the script looks for it.
  3. If you cannot share it, for example for privacy reasons, say so in the README, and explain where readers can get it and where to put it.

A script uses something it does not create or load itself.

  • 03_analysis.R: data_id

Usually the object was still in your R session from earlier work, or another script made it.

  1. Restart R (in RStudio: Session > Restart R).
  2. Run each script from top to bottom, and fix what is missing.
  3. If a script needs results of another, save them to a file in the first script and read them in the second.
  4. Load every package with library() at the top.

Metacheck can’t automatically establish what caused the error, or how it should be improved.

  • 01_literatureSearch.R

The error message of each script is in the table above.

All details of the Reproducibility Check

This module assesses whether the paper’s code could be run on its data, and — because execute = TRUE — actually ran it. We examined 4 R code files.

Run order

The scripts were ordered by their data dependencies (a script writing a file another reads runs first), source() calls, and numeric filename prefixes.

2 02_cleaningIPD.R — numeric
3 03_analysis.R — numeric
4 04_plotting.r 03_analysis.R dependency

File paths

9 data paths in the code do not work in the repository as deposited. We pointed them to where the file is, so the code could run: ./02_data/01_LiteratureSearch/EligibleStudies.csv to ../02_data/01_LiteratureSearch/EligibleStudies.csv (in 02_cleaningIPD.R); TableS5_AgeSlopeModerators.xlsx to 02_data/03_analysis/Supplement_tables/TableS5_AgeSlopeModerators.xlsx (in 03_analysis.R); TableS6_GenderSlopeModerators.xlsx to 02_data/03_analysis/Supplement_tables/TableS6_GenderSlopeModerators.xlsx (in 03_analysis.R); TableS7_EducationSlopeModerators.xlsx to 02_data/03_analysis/Supplement_tables/TableS7_EducationSlopeModerators.xlsx (in 03_analysis.R); TableS10_AdditiveModelWithoutFlags.xlsx to 02_data/03_analysis/Supplement_tables/TableS10_AdditiveModelWithoutFlags.xlsx (in 03_analysis.R); TableS11_ExtendedModelWithoutFlags.xlsx to 02_data/03_analysis/Supplement_tables/TableS11_ExtendedModelWithoutFlags.xlsx (in 03_analysis.R); AnalysisResults_full.RData to 02_data/AnalysisResults_full.RData (in 04_plotting.r); IPD_data.RDS to 02_data/IPD_data.RDS (in 04_plotting.r); normality_statistics.csv to 02_data/03_analysis/Supplement_tables/normality_statistics.csv (in 04_plotting.r). The code should be changed, because as written it does not find these files. 6 data paths were built at runtime with sprintf()/paste()/file.path() instead of written as a literal path — this is fragile authoring practice (it silently breaks if the code is run from a different working directory than the author’s own). We resolved all of these on a best-effort basis.

Files the deposit does not hold

The scripts that did not run through read 17 data files that are not in the deposit, and no script of the deposit writes: covid_within_t1.csv, covid_between_t1.csv, covid_between_t2.csv, covid_between_t3.csv, headers_de_t1.csv, headers_de_t2.csv, headers_de_t3.csv, selfuniqueness.data.sav, comp op data 6-15-23.sav, data_wide_full.csv, w1_pandrisk.rdata, salvador-casara_et_al_2022_covid-19_vaccination_intentions_network_approach_suppl_study1_data.csv, salvador-casara_et_al_2022_covid-19_vaccination_intentions_network_approach_suppl_study2_data.csv, data_decastro.csv, study_2_data.csv, study_3_data.csv, study_3_demographics_from_jasp.csv.

Execution

The code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 4 scripts: 1 ran without error, 3 errored, 0 timed out, 0 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse. Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions. A script wrote into 2 folders that the deposit does not have, so we made them and ran it once more: 03_figures/qq_plots for 04_plotting.r; 03_figures/sample_distributions for 04_plotting.r. Keeping the (empty) output folders in the deposit, or making them in the code with dir.create(), solves this.

Undefined-variable errors

1 script failed on an undefined variable or function (object '...' not found / could not find function "..."). This typically means the script expects a variable or function that another script defines — i.e. it is meant to be sourced into a larger session, not run on its own — or the symbol is simply never created. When another of the paper’s own script files defines the same name, this is called out below as a likely sourcing/copy-paste gap. Each is counted as an error (red).

03_analysis.R data_id (not defined anywhere in the paper’s code)

More detail

Ethics Approval Check

The paper does not appear to report data about individual people or animals (we found: a review or meta-analysis named in the title or abstract; a literature search; coding of published papers; a statement that there are no data), so we do not expect an ethics statement.

We based this on:

Although, on average, comparative optimism was observed (d = 0.334, 95% CI [0.225, 0.444]), true effects varied substantially, and the meta-analytic prediction interval ranged from -0.371 to 1.040.

We sought both individual participant data (IPD) and aggregate data (AD).

When IPD could not be obtained, studies remained eligible when sufficient aggregate statistics were reported to calculate a standardized effect size.

Power Analysis Check

No power analyses were detected.

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen’s d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.
